newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds to look for a slide towards 100.28.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds to look for a slide towards 100.28.

text.p: June Bund futures traded on LIFFE will continue to look negative on Tuesday and will head for major support at 100.28, technical analysts said.

"Bunds failed to get very far on Friday after the mid-week falls and from this morning's open they are still looking vulnerable to a support band at 100.62, 54 and below that the next really big support is at 100.28," said David Wood, an independent analyst near London.
On daily charts 100.28 was the low on April 25.
At 0658 GMT, June Bund futures were at 100.70, down 30 basis points on the day, having slipped from 100.81 at the open.
The initial support area at 100.62 to 100.54 was from previous swings and projections, Wood said.
"There is a heaviness over the long end which looks like it will continue probably without too much to turn it around in the way of news and market events this week," he said.
To the upside, Wood said the contract would start to hit problems around 100.90 to 101.04.
That area incorporates the April 15 high at 100.90, and more recently the May 21 low at 100.95 and Friday's high at 101.04.
"Really it has got to get up through 101.15 to 25 to turn this trend around," Wood said.
Guenter Redeker, technical analyst at Chase in London, also said Bunds were likely to head lower on Tuesday.

"There will be a key level for today at 100.63, the low tested on Thursday. There could be some corrective activity today from there but then we need to get above 100.99 to open up potential to 101.05," he said.
The contract formed a high at 101.05 on April 24. Above there, Redeker said 101.20 was likely to be the maximum for now.
"That level is defined by upper trendline resistance of a downward sloping channel and the market will look pretty tired at that level," he said.
Redeker said a downside break of 100.63 would lead to further selling pressure to test trendline suppport at 100.40.
"If we get below 100.28 the market would have to test 100.00 and then 99.70, both of which are Elliott levels," he said.
At the short end, September Euromarks were at 96.73, unchanged on the day.
